subject: ShortPilot phased on-ramp & credit routing
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya@lucenthealth.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@lucenthealth.com
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: ShortPilot bridge options and on-ramp

Hi Kimberly / Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the engineers were able to run a few experiments and we want to keep momentum. We have a short pilot (time-boxed) running out later this month and would like to discuss two things: a) a 3-week bridge to give us extra runway while we finalize the internal PO, and b) an approach for a phased on-ramp so we can scale throughput as model usage grows.

Attached is a small usage snapshot from our pilot so you can see spike patterns: [attachment: pilot-usage-summary.csv (CSV, 12KB)]. Our procurement team prefers either an invoice for the 3-week top-up or a one-off credit applied to our account — we are flexible but need a clear path for accounting.

Can you outline options (pricing, timing, contract addendum) and what you need from us to move quickly? We want minimal gaps in availability.

—Maya
Maya Patel
Head of ML Platforms, Lucent Health
maya@lucenthealth.com

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@lucenthealth.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, procurement@lucenthealth.com
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ShortPilot bridge options and on-ramp

Hi Maya — thanks for the usage snapshot. Quick summary of practical pathways below and what we'd need to finalize: 

Option A — 3-week timebox (invoice):
- We invoice Lucent for a fixed 3-week runway at the trial rate.
- During that period we keep the same concurrency and can reserve burst capacity.
- This is straightforward for procurement but will require an amendment to the existing trial SOW so Finance has an invoice reference.
- Impact: immediate access, no changes to account credits.

Option B — One-off credit bucket (preferred for accounting flexibility):
- We apply a pre-paid credit to your account that covers the same token/throughput envelope as the 3-week invoice.
- Credits are redeemable during the pilot extension; unused credits roll into normal billing for 30 days (can be constrained if you prefer).
- Advantage: no extra invoice process; easier to reconcile against usage.

Phased on-ramp suggestion (recommended):
- Week 0–1: Maintain current concurrency (safety baseline).
- Week 1–2: Open a controlled burst window (x2 concurrency) for scheduled test runs.
- Week 2–3: Full burst capacity enabled with an agreed throttling policy + alert thresholds.

What we need from Lucent to proceed:
1) Procurement preference (invoice vs credit).
2) PO or billing contact + billing address.
3) Any procurement/legal redlines for a short addendum (if invoice route).

I attached a short proposal that lays out numbers and the addendum language we typically use: [attachment: proposal-3wk-vs-credit.pdf]. Priyom — should we propose the 10% one-time credit incentive if they commit to the convert plan by 9/10?

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[kimberly_park@redwood.com]

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@lucenthealth.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ShortPilot bridge options and on-ramp

Maya — quick follow from my side: we can do Option B (credit) with an additional one-time 10% top-up credit if Lucent signs a short convert commitment (6 months) by end-of-day 2026-09-10.

Structure I recommend:
- 3-week credit bucket sized to projected usage (see Kimberly's proposal).
- If committed conversion is signed by 9/10, apply +10% bonus credit and tier a modest discount on month 1 usage.
- If no commitment, credit still applies but without bonus.

I'll draft the commit language and pricing table if you want to present both options to procurement.

—Priyom
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Procurement Team <procurement@lucenthealth.com>

Subject: Re: ShortPilot bridge options and on-ramp

Hi Kimberly / Priyom,

Thanks — procurement here. A couple items before we can agree to either invoice or credit:
- We need to route any invoice/PO against our master vendor record and will need Redwood's W-9 and vendor address.
- For credits, we require a short addendum to the existing MSA that specifies credit accounting and expiration terms.
- Also attached is our vendor security questionnaire — please confirm SOC 2 type II and data residency details for pilot data.

Attached: [attachment: vendor-security-questions.pdf]

If you can provide these items and a sample addendum, we can issue a PO quickly.

Regards,
Lucent Health Procurement
procurement@lucenthealth.com

Procurement team — thanks for the checklist. Notes below and next steps: 

1) Vendor paperwork: we will send W-9 and vendor address to your AP contact by EOD.
2) Addendum: attached proposal includes the short addendum language we typically use for short pilot credits (see file). If you prefer invoice route we can convert the same language into an invoice SOW.
3) Security: Redwood can provide the SOC 2 Type II report and an extract of our data handling practices for trial data. For this short pilot we can enable account-level logging and exportable audit logs; we do not require a Private deployment.

DocuSign: I've created a DocuSign addendum for the credit path — link here: https://www.docusign.com/ADDENDUM_LINK_123
HubSpot: deal is LD-2026-091 if you want to review the commercial terms: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/LD-2026-091

If you confirm the credit route, we'll apply the 3-week credit immediately on receipt of a PO or signature on the addendum. Priyom — I included your commit incentive language; if Lucent signs by 9/10 we apply the +10% bonus credit.

Best,
Kimberly
